faq.question: What is an AI agent platform?
faq.answer: A centralized environment to build, manage, and govern AI agents securely across different business processes.

faq.question: Which types of agents can run on the platform?
faq.answer: SAP, ERP, browser, RPA, and autonomous agents.

faq.question: How do you control what an agent is allowed to do?
faq.answer: Through strict permissions, access controls, and validation rules defined during setup.

faq.question: Can humans review or approve agent actions?

faq.question: Which SAP environments can Agentfloww automate?
faq.answer: Agentfloww is designed to integrate with SAP Business One, SAP S/4HANA, and other enterprise systems via approved integration layers, subject to discovery.

faq.question: Can SAP automation include human approval steps?
faq.answer: Yes. Defined workflows can include controlled validation gates and human-in-the-loop approvals before any write-back occurs.

faq.question: How do you validate transactions before write-back?
faq.answer: Validation rules are mapped during implementation. The agent checks data against these rules and surfaces exceptions for human review before execution.

faq.question: What happens when the automation encounters an exception?
faq.answer: When an exception or edge case is detected, the agent safely halts the specific task and escalates it to the appropriate human team for review.

faq.question: Can an SAP automation pilot start with one workflow?
faq.answer: Yes. We recommend starting with a single, well-defined workflow in a safe environment before expanding across approved processes.

faq.question: What makes an AI agent autonomous?
faq.answer: An autonomous agent can plan multi-step tasks and intelligently select tools to achieve a defined business goal, rather than just following strict linear rules.

faq.question: Can autonomous agents work across multiple systems?
faq.answer: Yes, they can coordinate workflows across email, documents, and approved enterprise systems, subject to discovery.

faq.question: How do you control what an agent is allowed to do?
faq.answer: Governance is established through strict permissions and validation gates that define exactly which actions the agent can take.

faq.question: When does a human take over?
faq.answer: Human reviewers take over during defined approval gates or whenever the agent encounters an ambiguous decision or exception.

faq.question: Can autonomous agents be deployed for one workflow first?
faq.answer: Yes. Deploying for a single workflow allows teams to map rules and test edge cases in a controlled path to production.

rpa-ai-agent.problemH2: Not every workflow can be handled by fixed rules alone
rpa-ai-agent.problemText: Traditional RPA works well for predictable, rule-based tasks. Business workflows can also contain documents, natural-language inputs and exceptions. An RPA AI Agent approach combines deterministic automation with AI capabilities where interpretation is required.

rpa-ai-agent.integrationsText: Can complement existing RPA tools, ERP systems, browser workflows, email, documents and APIs, subject to the target environment.

faq.question: When should we use RPA AI instead of traditional RPA?
faq.answer: RPA AI is ideal when a workflow involves variable inputs, document understanding, or decisions that require context rather than rigid rules.

faq.question: Can an RPA AI agent work with existing automation?
faq.answer: Yes, it can complement and connect with existing RPA tools and workflows, subject to the technical environment.

faq.question: How are AI decisions validated?
faq.answer: Decisions are validated against defined business rules, and any edge cases are routed to a human for confirmation.

faq.question: Can the system escalate uncertain cases?
faq.answer: Yes. Clear escalation protocols ensure that uncertain tasks cannot proceed without human intervention.

faq.question: Can we modernize an existing RPA workflow gradually?
faq.answer: Yes. You can isolate specific interpretation steps in a workflow to pilot AI capabilities while keeping the rest of the process deterministic.
